solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Battle walker devised to get flan

indicators.note: something devised is worked out afresh, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A war veteran's walk is cooked up into a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges all twelve letters of BATTLE WALKER; 'to get' is the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond and jam pastry from Derbyshire is a classic open tart, a kind of flan.

clue.text: Show anger in English city after expulsion of old English

indicators.note: expulsion means throwing out, so the letter for old is removed from the city's name

parts.note: Bristol is a city in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry in a city once an elderly Englishman has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from BRISTOL leaves BRISTL, and E goes on the end; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to react with visible irritation, like an animal raising its hackles.

clue.text: Smart Alec close to desk describing open-plan office?

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: an open-plan office has no wall dividing it, read as two words

explanation.surface: A clever clogs sits near a desk in an office without partitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' joins the pieces; the question mark flags the playful reading of an open-plan office as one with NO WALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal labels for an irritating person who thinks they have all the answers.

clue.text: Doctor taken in by trick put on in London suburb

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so the doctor goes within the trick

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A medic is fooled by a ruse staged in an outer part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts the doctor inside the trick; 'Doctor' tempts as DR, but MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is needed. 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This district of south-west London, home of the tennis championships, is a suburb of the capital.

clue.text: Fruit I found overlooking church among couple of limes

indicators.note: being among things means sitting in their midst, so the pieces go inside
a couple means two, so the first two letters of the word are taken
in a down clue a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

explanation.surface: I spot some fruit by a church set amid a pair of lime trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts the I-over-church piece inside the first two letters of 'limes'; 'found' is a link. LICHI is a variant spelling of lychee.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichi, also spelt lychee, is a small sweet Chinese fruit with a rough red skin.

clue.text: Line in brown followed by fellow

indicators.note: a piece followed by another has that other placed after it

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A line runs through a brown area, with a man coming after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is just a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: Composer with diva in Italy

parts.note: Diana Ross is a famous diva of soul and pop
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer works alongside an opera prima donna in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian composer of The Barber of Seville and William Tell.

clue.text: Club, perhaps, with national language correctly used

parts.note: Queen's Club is a well-known London tennis club, so it is one example of a club
English describes the nationality of someone from England

explanation.surface: A sports club adopts the country's tongue, spoken properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club, perhaps' is a definition by example: Queen's Club hosts a tennis tournament in west London. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names standard, correct British speech and writing.

clue.text: Notorious criminal? Raise person travelling to protect ambassador

parts.note: to jack up a car is to raise it

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: a tripper is someone on a trip or excursion
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A traveller lifts a car to shield a diplomat from danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notorious criminal?' with its question mark admits a definition by example; 'to protect' wraps the traveller round the ambassador's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The unidentified Whitechapel murderer of 1888 is history's most infamous unsolved killer.

clue.text: Distinctive garb shown by two educational bodies?

parts.note: uni is short for university, one place of learning
a form is a school class, another group in education

explanation.surface: Two schools share a distinctive outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is a link; the one phrase supplies both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn identically by members of a group is a standard outfit identifying them.

clue.text: Players keeping article introducing a card game

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the article goes within

parts.note: the cast of a play is its players
an is the indefinite article
the letter a is taken as written, with introducing placing what comes before it in front

explanation.surface: Actors bring a little something to start a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts the article between the first two and last two letters of the players' word; 'introducing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style game played with two packs, a card game from South America.

clue.text: Part of animal later in ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of beast is later put through the mincer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil or minced meat, but it rearranges LATER IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrail is one of the internal organs or guts of a creature.

clue.text: Reserve select item for very wintry weather?

parts.note: ice means cold reserve or aloofness in manner
to pick is to select

explanation.surface: Choosing kit to stock up for severe winter conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a playful definition: an ice pick suits conditions where everything is frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: This pointed tool for breaking frozen water fits extremely cold conditions, a whimsical description.

clue.text: Bulge shown by bigwig

definitions.meaning: to bulge is to expand outward
a fashionable or important person, an old slang word for a toff

explanation.surface: A big shot shows a protruding paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to grow larger outwardly and, informally, a stylish upper-class person.

clue.text: Wrong lead taken by fool initially hopelessly attended to

indicators.note: something done wrong is put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a twit is a silly person, a fool

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A misled fool hopelessly follows the wrong lead.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL comes from rearranging LEAD; 'taken by' links it to TWIT and the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing with a problem means handling it, having seen to or taken care of it.

clue.text: A huge amount designed reportedly in urban growth area?

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a similar-sounding word

parts.note: a lot is a huge amount and meant is designed or intended

explanation.surface: A vast amount of money set aside for an area of city development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urban growth area?' looks like suburban sprawl, but it is a town vegetable plot; 'in' is a link. An ALLOTMENT is a rented UK patch for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land rented for growing produce, often in towns, is literally a place where things grow.

clue.text: Number with spell in state in the small hours?

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
a turn is a spell or shift on duty

explanation.surface: A number takes a stint in a US state during the early hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the spell inside the abbreviated US state; 'with' is a link. The question mark marks a playful definition: active in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something active at night, such as an owl, does its business in the hours after midnight.

clue.text: Use up whole amount pocketed by cold individual

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: something pocketed by another is held inside it

parts.note: one means a single individual
a sum is a total, the whole amount

explanation.surface: A cold loner pockets the whole sum and spends it.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM goes inside CONE after CON to give CONSUME.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume resources is to exhaust or spend them completely.

clue.text: Tense point with one interrupting rampaging thug

indicators.note: something interrupting another breaks into it, so the pieces go inside
rampaging means running wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nervy moment as someone tries to stop a violent thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like grammar but is the adjective for nervy; 'rampaging' scrambles the thug and 'interrupting' breaks into it after its first letter; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uptight means being anxious and on edge, the nervous sense of tense.

clue.text: Band of singers in some papers reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is spoken aloud to give a near-identical sound

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: The press covers a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests a pop group, but it means any group; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group who sing together, especially in church.

clue.text: Anglican name bound to get criticism

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: A churchman is certain to be criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is formal disapproval, a strong expression of criticism.

clue.text: One shunned in published group, we hear

parts.note: a book that is out has been published

indicators.note: we hear marks a word spoken, sounding like the one entered

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social group

explanation.surface: Someone excluded from a well-known circle, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; CAST is the spelling entered for CASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected and avoided by society.

clue.text: Nuts at one in curtailed meal

indicators.note: one piece inside another goes within it
curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone eats nuts at a shortened lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food to match the meal, but it is the adjective for mad. LUNCH loses H to give LUNC, which takes AT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal adjectives meaning crazy or out of one's mind.

clue.text: King supporting college? That's evident

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other, so it comes after

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch props up a university, which is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear means obvious or plain to understand, a synonym of evident.

clue.text: Fail to pick originally knitted garment

parts.note: to tank is informal for to fail badly

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Failing to choose originally a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: A tank top is a sleeveless knitted pullover worn over a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: This sleeveless pullover, worn over a shirt, is typically knitted.

clue.text: Run without being noticed?

parts.note: to run goods is to carry contraband, and doing it unobserved is the illegal import trade

explanation.definitionFit: Bringing contraband in secretly is running goods past customs undetected.

clue.text: Train due for renovation caught at start of evening

indicators.note: renovation is a making over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A train due for a refit is caught at the start of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway train, but it is the verb; DUE becomes EDU.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach or instruct them, the sense of educate.

clue.text: Live with a group of volunteers by convent and avoid unpleasantness?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
a convent is a religious retreat

explanation.surface: Living with volunteers next to a nunnery to escape trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with', 'by' and 'and' are links. The TA was the British Army's reserve of part-time volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw from a difficult situation is to escape something disagreeable, the idiom's sense.
